title: Daily Markets Comment, Day 1
subtitle: Daily commentary from Yash
body:
Good afternoon from Frankfurt. 
It’s been a while since I left so I’m excited to see what I missed. 

Today’s comment will cover broader risk sentiment and price action since I’m looking at things where they are for now.

Equity 
Major indices in the US have hit recent all time highs. It’s surprising to see why? Similarly is the case for most of the indices from the Asia and EU. I wonder why that might be. SPX is standing tall at 7700, a level I’m not comfortable at. The rally perhaps will hit breaks. Were it the blockbuster earning seasons again? 

FX
EUR is down from YTD highs although started rallying again last month after the 27th. It isn’t surprising though because of broader risk on sentiment. JPY is looking interesting, it rallied during the same week that of EUR. YTD JPY remains weaker but the trend to the upside is continuing. Cable and Aussie seem to be choppy and CHF is quietly weakening. 

Commodities 
Mr. Gold had a huge rally this week. It’s still lower YTD but I wonder if the recent reversal is sustainable. You know these bounce back are usually part of the bigger trend. Crude oil reversing too, I’m suspecting some deal that’s been promised or perhaps it’s the trump talking? Either way my outlook for the crude oil remains strong to the upside. The war changed how markets view the supply chain risk forever and every country saw a mighty nation not being able to negotiate. Supply chains aren’t restored overnight so price action shouldn’t either.

Rates / Credit	
US are topping all time highs and it seems as if inflation expectations are fully priced in at the moment. The September 16th meeting is expected to hold rates but I think a case for tightening might be coming. 

Top Headlines, 
SpaceX falling after good earnings report. 
SPX hitting all time highs. 
Iran proposals to have control traffic of the Strait of Hormuz in the US-Iran deal. 

End thought
Broader risk on sentiment. A falling of a few single equity names. FX markets with JPY setting up for a trade. Rate hike expectations in the US baking in.
